chain.label: PF inadequately trained in visual approaches and manual flight
chain.trigger: "the PF's inadequate training on the planning and execution of visual approaches"

chain.label: Asiana/Boeing autoflight training, documentation and automation policy inadequate
chain.trigger: "the complexities of the autothrottle and autopilot flight director systems that were inadequately described in Boeing's documentation and Asiana's pilot training"

chain.label: 777 A/T provides no low-speed protection in HOLD mode after FLCH override
chain.trigger: "When in HOLD mode, the A/T will not wake up even during large deviations from target speed and does not support stall protection"

chain.label: Flight crew fatigued from circadian disruption and fragmented sleep
chain.trigger: "the accident occurred during the pilots' circadian trough"; PF obtained about 5.5 hours of sleep in the prior 24 hours

chain.label: Crew mismanaged descent, leaving airplane far above glidepath at 5 nm
chain.trigger: "the flight crew mismanaged the airplane's descent, which resulted in the airplane being well above the desired 3° glidepath when it reached the 5 nm point"

caused_by.evidence: "The PF's lack of exposure in 777 transition training to straight-in speed-restricted visual approaches played a role in the flight crew's mismanagement of the airplane's vertical profile"
"each made errors that were consistent with the effects of fatigue"

chain.label: Nonstandard callouts, role confusion and inadequate instructor supervision
chain.trigger: "the flight crew's nonstandard communication and coordination regarding the use of the autothrottle and autopilot flight director systems"

caused_by.evidence: "The PM did not have the opportunity during his instructor training to supervise and instruct a trainee during line operations while being observed by an experienced instructor"
"all three pilots were likely fatigued as a result of circadian disruption"

chain.label: PF selected FLCH SPD, disconnected A/P and manually pulled thrust levers to idle
chain.trigger: "the pilot flying (PF) selected an autopilot (A/P) mode (flight level change speed [FLCH SPD]) that instead resulted in the autoflight system initiating a climb...The PF disconnected the A/P and moved the thrust levers to idle"

caused_by.evidence: "The PF was aware of the need to lose excess altitude and attempted to do so using FLCH SPD pitch mode"
"the PF had an inaccurate understanding of how the AFDS and A/T interacted to control airspeed, which led to his inadvertent deactivation of automatic airspeed control"
"manually overriding the throttle levers during a climb in FLCH SPD pitch mode changes the A/T operating mode from THR to HOLD. This inconsistency increases the opportunity for pilot error"

chain.label: A/T transitioned to HOLD; automatic airspeed control deactivated with thrust at idle
chain.trigger: "the thrust levers reached the idle position, and the A/T mode changed to HOLD" — a mode in which the A/T does not control airspeed

caused_by.evidence: "As a result of the PF's manual override of the A/T, the A/T mode switched to HOLD, a mode in which the A/T would not move the thrust levers and was not controlling thrust or airspeed"

"if the A/T automatic engagement function ('wakeup'), or a system with similar functionality, had been available during the final approach, it would likely have activated and increased power about 20 seconds before impact"
"the two F/D switches were not both in the off position at the same time. If they had been, the A/T mode would have changed to speed mode and maintained the approach speed of 137 knots"

chain.label: Crew failed to monitor airspeed as it decayed below Vref
chain.trigger: "insufficient flight crew monitoring of airspeed indications during the approach likely resulted from expectancy, increased workload, fatigue, and automation reliance"

caused_by.evidence: "the PF, PM, and observer believed the A/T system was controlling speed with thrust, they had a high degree of trust in the automated system, and they did not closely monitor these parameters"
"This increased workload was created, in part, by task compression resulting from the flight crew's ineffective management of vertical path earlier in the approach"
"it is also possible that his monitoring performance, and that of the other flight crewmembers, was degraded by fatigue"

chain.label: Airspeed decayed to 103 knots and airplane sank well below glidepath
chain.trigger: "the PAPI indication changed to four red lights, showing the airplane's significantly below-glidepath position"; lowest airspeed about 103 knots

caused_by.evidence: "the thrust levers were still at idle, and the descent rate was about 1,200 ft per minute, well above the descent rate of about 700 fpm needed to maintain the desired glidepath"
"The decreasing trend in airspeed continued, and about 200 ft, the flight crew became aware of the low airspeed and low path conditions"

chain.label: Mandatory go-around not initiated at 500 ft and delayed until below 100 ft
chain.trigger: "the flight crew's delayed execution of a go-around after they became aware that the airplane was below acceptable glidepath and airspeed tolerances"

caused_by.evidence: "Based on these two indications, the flight crew should have determined that the approach was unstabilized and initiated a go-around, but they did not do so"
"they did not initiate a go-around until the airplane was below 100 ft, at which point the airplane did not have the performance capability to accomplish a go-around"
"the delayed initiation of a go-around by the PF and the PM...likely resulted from a combination of surprise, nonstandard communication, and role confusion"

chain.label: Stick shaker activated on short final at high angle of attack
chain.trigger: "the CVR recorded the stick shaker activating, and the lowest airspeed during the approach of about 103 knots was recorded by the FDR"

caused_by.evidence: "the airspeed was about 114 knots"...decaying to about 103 knots with pitch attitude reaching about 12° nose up
"the control column reached the full aft position, and the stall warning stick shaker activated" after the belated thrust increase

chain.label: Main gear and aft fuselage struck the seawall short of runway 28L
chain.trigger: "The initial impact with the seawall occurred at 1127:50"; the tail broke off and the airplane slid, spun about 330°, and impacted the ground again

caused_by.evidence: "a go-around that was initiated 11 seconds before the impact (at an altitude of 124 ft) likely would not have resulted in the ground impact"
"engines were increasing through about 92%, and the airspeed was about 106 knots" at impact, the airplane having no performance capability to arrest the descent

chain.label: Three passengers fatally injured, 49 serious injuries; airplane destroyed by impact and fire
chain.trigger: "Three of the 291 passengers were fatally injured; 40 passengers, 8 of the 12 flight attendants, and 1 of the 4 flight crewmembers received serious injuries"

caused_by.evidence: "The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire"; two unrestrained passengers were "ejected through the ruptured tail of the airplane" during the impact sequence
